title: Allow policies, deny policies and how inheritance resolves

videos.script: Every resource carries one allow policy. It is a list of bindings, and each binding joins a role to the principals that hold it. {{bindings}} A policy is never edited in place. A client reads it, changes its copy, and writes the whole thing back. {{rmw}} So two people can overwrite each other. The etag is what stops that. Google refuses a write made from a copy that is out of date. {{etag}} Terraform has three ways to own a policy. The whole policy. One role. Or one grant. The first two remove whatever the file does not name. {{three}} And their plans look the same, which is the danger. {{alike}} Then there is the other kind of policy. Allow policies add up down the tree, and nothing lower down can take a grant away. {{union}} A deny policy can. It is read first, and if it refuses, nothing else is read. {{deny}} You will plan one for production. Nobody deletes the project. Except a break-glass group. {{end}}
